messages:
Priya K: Quick sync — ran the graceful-degrade slot coordination sim against last week's spike pattern. TL;DR: 18% cost drop vs baseline, p95 up ~3% and a small p99 tail when preemption is aggressive. Need a decision on preemption ordering + admission control.

Alex W: Can you paste the sim config and the failure scenarios you ran?

Priya K: posted config and shorthand results below:
```
slot_strategy: staggered_soft_preempt
preempt_threshold: 0.7    # fraction of slot usage to trigger preempt
fairness_window: 30s
hedge_policy: disabled
traffic_profile: spike-2026-03-14
failure_modes: [node_drain, gpu_lost, high_latency_surge]
metrics: [p50,p95,p99,cost_per_token,success_rate]
```

Priya K: results summary: cost_per_token -18%, p95 +3%, p99 +6% (only during node_drain + all-heavy-slot-preempt), success_rate unchanged ~99.98%

Sam L: okay that p99 cliff sounds bad. Is that the case where we preempt N heavy slots at once so everything falls back to slower replicas?

Priya K: yes. scenario: several tenant slots flagged high-cost -> scheduler preempts them in same epoch -> warm KV caches cold -> a burst of cold KV lookups + model swap -> short p99 spike.

Lee H: two axes to consider: ordering and stagger. We can do either (A) soft-preempt: evict less aggressively and allow fairness_window so not all heavy slots are reclaimed at once, or (B) hard-preempt + immediate hedging to a compatible lower-cost model.

Maria P: also measure request-level success vs user-visible error. If p99 latency goes from 220ms -> 330ms but no errors, product might accept that if cost saving is material. Need product consult.

Alex W: mathematically, if preempt fraction f and slot count S, expected cold-cache rate ~ 1 - (1 - f)^{S} which explains non-linear tail. Staggering reduces concurrent cold events.

Priya K: Suggested options to pick from: 
- Option 1: Staggered soft-preempt + fairness_window=30s + aggressive batching watch (lowers concurrency)
- Option 2: Hard preempt but auto-hedge to warm smaller model + promote back when capacity returns
- Option 3: Hybrid: soft-preempt by default, escalate to hard if cumulative preempt rate > X within Ys

Sam L: what about admission control? If we throttle new low-priority load during reclaim, that reduces the p99 cost of cold misses.

Priya K: yep we tried admission throttle at 30% new-request drop for low-tier tenants in sim; that removed most of p99 tail but reduced throughput for those tenants. tradeoff: SLA hit vs aggregate unit cost.

Lee H: implementation surface: soft-preempt needs tracking windows in scheduler, fairness metadata on slots, and a token-bucket to pace evictions. Hard-preempt needs reliable model-variant map + quick fallbacks. Both require telemetry hooks.

Maria P: can we do a short canary? Roll soft-preempt to 5% of capacity with full tracing for 48h and run the same spike generator. Product + SRE to sign-off.

infra-bot: deploy request created: PR#4821 -> staging policy-experiments/staggered-soft-preempt (link: https://git.internal/r/redwood/pr/4821) :robot_face:

Alex W: my vote is Option 3 (hybrid). Start soft, have clear escalation thresholds, and require hedging-paths tested. Also add admission-control knobs.

Sam L: +1 to hybrid. Also add a safety valve: if p99 > threshold for N minutes, rollback policy automatically.

Maria P: +1 for canary + hybrid. I'll coordinate with product to sign the tolerance matrix for p95/p99 vs cost.

Priya K: Next steps:
- Priya: implement fairness_window + pacing token-bucket (ETA: 1 week)
- Alex: add math model + threshold calc for escalation (ETA: 3 days)
- Lee: prototype hedging path and warmup hooks (ETA: 2 weeks)
- Sam: add auto-rollback SLO detector to oncall runbooks (ETA: 4 days)
- Maria: coordinate product signoff and canary schedule (ETA: 2 business days)

Priya K: we'll run canary on Wednesday spike window and reconvene Thu 10am PT. If any objections file on the PR or ping me. :thumbsup:

Lee H: nit: capture cost-savings attribution per-tenant so we can opt-out noisy tenants during canary.

Priya K: noted. adding per-tenant attribution to the canary matrix.

Alex W: thanks — this feels actionable.

Maria P: thanks all :sparkles:

Priya K: ending thread with checklist created in PR comments.
